text:
Situation: Diltiazem hydrochloride injection has been on FDA's shortage list for 104 months as of 2026-10-21. Hospira, Inc., a Pfizer Company, discontinued manufacture with an initial posting date of 2026-01-05. Current stock at Corvale East and Corvale General provides 9.3 to 23 days of supply across formulations.

Why (FDA record): FDA's shortage list shows the product status as To Be Discontinued since 2018-02-21. The product label for NDC 00409435003 names Hospira, Inc. (FEI 1925262) as the manufacturing plant. FDA inspection 976095 at that plant ended 2016-06-08 and was classified OAI, 623 days before the 2018-02-21 shortage posting. A Warning Letter was issued to the same plant on 2017-02-14, 372 days before the 2018-02-21 posting. FDA inspection 1064827 at the plant ended 2018-08-15 and was classified OAI, 175 days after the 2018-02-21 posting.

Our position: The rule‑based best option is to buy from HF Acquisition Co LLC, DBA HealthFirst, which is not on FDA's shortage list today. Four additional suppliers also are not on the shortage list. No plant information is available on their labels.

Recommended actions:
1. Buyer to initiate purchase from HF Acquisition Co LLC, DBA HealthFirst; requires Pharmacy Director approval.
2. Buyer to qualify Medical Purchasing Solutions, LLC as secondary source; requires Pharmacy Director approval.
3. Buyer to qualify ProPharma Distribution as tertiary source; requires Pharmacy Director approval.
4. Buyer to qualify Sagent Pharmaceuticals as quaternary source; requires Pharmacy Director approval.
5. Buyer to monitor FDA shortage list weekly and report changes to P&T Committee; requires P&T Committee Chair acknowledgment.

Not recommended: Delaying procurement while awaiting Hospira product return; the product is marked To Be Discontinued.
